analyst_view.overall: A Monday-night relegation derby of the Valencian region: Levante (17th, 11 pts, on the survival line after a 0-0 at Celta) host Elche (18th, 10 pts), who lost 2-0 at Betis and have not won an official game in Valencia since 1993; a win lifts Elche out of the drop zone. Luís Castro's Levante have a near-empty injury list and no suspensions, with Manu Sánchez, Ryan, Iván Romero and Bardeli back. Anselmi's Elche miss Marc Aguado, while Houary (in the numbers) is still out and Yago de Santiago and Boayar are doubts; Villar, Sangaré and Lemar are back, though Lemar may not start. No referee has been named in the pages I read as of Sunday morning, and the numbers do not flag the derby.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already high for two bottom-four sides, because Levante concede a lot at home and Elche create plenty. Elche get Villar and Lemar back and Anselmi expects an attacking Levante, but Elche keep missing chances and a tense six-pointer can make both careful. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's. Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and cross for Fer Niño, which the numbers already see in their 31 corners in six games, while Levante have won fewer than expected lately. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I keep 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, low because Levante have been booked little lately (11 in six). This is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between sides a point apart, which the numbers do not flag, and Anselmi was prickly in his press conference about the pressure; games like that usually bring more fouls and bookings. No referee named yet, so a moderate lean up to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting (Levante conceded 103 in six games). Anselmi expects Levante to attack at home and Elche's possession game keeps the volume high, but a nervy six-pointer could also slow it down. Nothing points clearly either way, so I keep 29.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Brugué and Fer Niño, each side's main scorer, are fit, Levante have a near-full squad and Villar's return gives Elche more control, though Anselmi admits their finishing has let them down. I keep 8.9.
